title: Langmuir kinetics and totally asymmetric volume exclusion in linear chains via Fock space formalism
summary: Driven-diffusive systems combining spatial exclusion and bulk exchange, such as the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process coupled with Langmuir kinetics (TASEP-LK), serve as foundational models for particle transport in vehicular traffic, conveyor networks, and mesoscopic flow channels. In this work, we employ an exact Doi-Peliti field-theoretic operator formulation in Fock space to evaluate steady-state observables, continuous phase landscapes, and spatial correlations in finite linear chains up to $k = 16$. By introducing a decomposition in terms of biorthonormal eigenvectors for asymmetric non-Hermitian matrices, the stationary state is calculated directly from the kernel of the quasi-Hamiltonian, completely bypassing the computationally prohibitive complexity of full matrix diagonalization and time-dependent matrix exponentiation. Across distinct rate regimes and global parametric scans, our exact discrete calculations demonstrate that finite-size stochastic fluctuations naturally smear out singular domain walls, producing smooth density profiles and continuous phase crossovers. Finite-size scaling illustrates how local profiles systematically steepen toward the sharp domain wall predicted by continuum field theory as $k \to \infty$. Furthermore, two-point correlation analysis reveals that in slow-kinetics regimes, spatial fluctuations generate strong inter-site cumulants, causing standard mean-field approximations to systematically underestimate joint occupancy probabilities by 50\%. These findings emphasize the necessity of analytical methods for modeling mesoscopic transport systems and short traffic corridors where local stochastic fluctuations and spatial correlations dominate the stationary dynamics.

title: Percolation of discorectangles oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions
comment: To be presented at The 10th International Scientific Conference The Modeling of Nonlinear Processes and Systems (MNPS-2026)
summary: The percolation of finite-thickness elongated objects---discorectangles (stadiums)---oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions is studied, extending recent results for zero-thickness sticks. The angular distribution is the ``Maltese cross'' parametrized by $α$. Based on the known analytic expression for the excluded area of a discorectangle pair, the percolation threshold is estimated by the eigenvalue method. The discorectangle connectivity matrix is represented as the stick matrix plus a rank-1 term determined by the constant part of the excluded area, $C=4lw+πw^{2}$, which gives the approximate relations $λ_{\max}^{\mathrm{DR}}\approxλ_{\max}^{\mathrm{stick}}+C$ and $n_c^{\mathrm{DR}}\approx n_c^{\mathrm{stick}}/(1+C n_c^{\mathrm{stick}})$. Finite thickness shifts the absolute thresholds and affects the first normalization, whereas the second normalization, written through maximum eigenvalues, cancels the additive geometric contribution and preserves only the orientational dependence, explaining the universality of the normalized curves. Monte Carlo simulations of unit-length discorectangles with aspect ratios 8, 16, and 32, various domain sizes, periodic boundary conditions, and union--find scaling analysis confirm the theoretical predictions.

title: Electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium: discretization and effective medium approximation
comment: To be presented at The 10th International Scientific Conference The Modeling of Nonlinear Processes and Systems (MNPS-2026)
summary: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is $σ_1$, $σ_2$, or the harmonic mean $σ_{12}=2σ_1σ_2/(σ_1+σ_2)$, with probabilities $(1-p)^2$, $p^2$, and $2p(1-p)$, respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity $x$ and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on $p$ and the conductivity ratio $r$. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a $200\times200$ resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of $1/2$. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.

title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
summary: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
comment: 27 pages, 23 figures: Letter (4 pages + End Matter, 3 figures) and Supplemental Material (20 figures)
summary: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench response fades, giving a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.

title: Confinement-induced bound state and effective potential for microwave-shielded ultracold molecules
summary: We investigate the bound state and effective potential of microwave-shielded ultracold molecules under longitudinal confinement, which effectively creates a quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) geometry. We find that the longitudinal confinement facilitates bound-state formation in both bosonic and fermionic molecules, leading to confinement-induced bound states that are absent in free space. To describe these bound states, we establish an effective 2D potential by incorporating the full interaction effect along the longitudinal direction. Compared with other simplified 2D potentials, the effective potential accurately predicts the binding energies of ultracold molecules over a much broader parameter regime of microwave coupling and confinement strength. Remarkably, it can even predict deep bound states with binding energies well exceeding the confinement frequency. By establishing this effective potential, our work paves the way for efficiently exploring the rich low-dimensional physics of microwave-shielded ultracold molecules.

title: Topological Transitions of Evanescent Waves
comment: 11 pages in main text, 26 pages in total, 6 Figures in main text, 7 Figures in total
summary: We study the band structure of evanescent waves, that is, the decaying or growing solutions that live within the gaps of tight-binding Hamiltonians. Although the underlying Hamiltonian is Hermitian, these modes carry complex wavevectors and therefore exhibit a non-Hermitian dispersion. Using the transfer matrix formalism in one dimension, we show that, in addition to the standard exceptional points that appear at the band edges, a different type of exceptional point can arise inside the gap, protected by spinless time-reversal symmetry. Tuning model parameters drives a topological transition where such in-gap exceptional points are nucleated in pairs, mediated by a crossing between purely imaginary momentum branches. We show that this spectral structure is diagnosed by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index assigned to every energy inside the gap, with the in-gap exceptional points arising as its domain walls. A generic bound state in the system has a tail that is purely exponential when its energy lies between a band edge and the nearest exceptional point, but becomes oscillatory - with a wavevector differing from the band-edge momentum - when its energy lies between the pair of in-gap exceptional points. We illustrate these results using continuum and tight-binding models, as well as an anisotropic photonic crystal.

title: Stability and Relaxation of Electron-Phonon Systems at Strong Coupling
summary: We study the kinetic properties of Migdal-Eliashberg theory (MET) for electron-phonon interactions at strong coupling. Previously, the system was found to be dynamically unstable at large couplings within a Markovian quantum Boltzmann approximation. Using the quasiclassical Kadanoff-Baym equation, we show that this instability is absent when non-Markovian effects are taken into account. We also analyze the long-time relaxation dynamics at strong-couplin, and find a clear imprint of the non-Markovian nature of the dynamics: in an intermediate temperature range between the Debye frequency and the coupling strength, the relaxation rate becomes linear in temperature with Planckian slope, while the leading relaxation mode acquires a large imaginary component, producing strongly oscillatory decay. Our results imply that any instability which preempts superconductivity must arise from effects beyond MET, such as phonon softening or polaronic effects at finite electronic bandwidth. This shows that the characteristic phonon frequency is not a fundamental bound on $T_c$, and leaves open a route to higher $T_c$ in multi-orbital electron-phonon systems.

title: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
summary: Quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation have been conjectured to offer up to a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods; however, the devil is always in the details. Here, we determine key physical conditions under which this quartic separation could be achieved in the relevant parameters. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order $m$, we find that the end-to-end speedup is of order $(m+4)/(m+1)$ in the simulation time, and $4/(m+1)$ in the accuracy, with exponential memory advantage. For elastic lattice systems, we define microscopically resolved bulk observables (MRBOs) as those that can be efficiently extracted from a quantum state, but cannot be resolved by a known continuum model with fewer degrees of freedom than the lattice. We then argue that the estimation of MRBOs is a candidate problem for quartic quantum advantage in problem size. We propose MRBOs for pseudorandom heterogeneous materials as an explicit end-to-end application where this occurs, while admitting efficient `quantum cheese' encodings of the material properties. We thus demonstrate how the interplay between regularity, physical scale, observable sensitivity and quantum encodability constrains the relation between classical and quantum complexity.

title: Emergent Symmetry in Constant-Density Flocks
summary: In two dimensions, the ordered phase of constant-density flocks is described by a single angle field, which makes them arguably the simplest systems with a scale-free ordered phase of collective motion. We show that the equation governing the corresponding Nambu-Goldstone mode, completed with terms previously discarded, possesses on large scales an invariance combining a shear and a Galilean boost. Broken at the bare level, this symmetry is restored at the unique attractive fixed point, and the associated Ward identities fix the scaling exponents exactly, as confirmed numerically.

title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
summary: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $Φ$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $Ω(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $Φ_{\rm p}(d)=Θ(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le Φ_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $Φ_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $Φ_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $Φ_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[Φ_{\rm d},Φ_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.

title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
summary: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

title: Parity-Selective Quantum Interference in Unconventional Magnets
summary: Nonrelativistic spin splitting has emerged as a defining feature of unconventional magnetic states. Here we show that quantum interference offers a symmetry-resolved probe for the parity of such spin splitting, as even- and odd-parity magnets exhibit qualitatively different weak (anti-)localization behaviors. Even-parity magnets can host time-reversal symmetric scattering loops depicted by the spin group, giving rise to a weak localization that can be suppressed by spin-orbit coupling. In contrast, odd-parity magnets have a hidden weak antilocalization that can be released by spinorbit coupling. We further derive the corresponding magnetoconductivity formulas to facilitate experimental explorations. Our results not only advance the weak (anti-)localization theory to unconventional magnets but also suggest a practical diagnostic of unconventional spin-split magnetic states.

title: Agnostic and efficient detection of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry-protected topological phases in projected entangled-pair states
summary: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are the simplest example of quantum phases that cannot be detected by local order parameters. Their classification is by now well-established from multiple perspectives, a prominent one being via tensor network states. The practical question, however, is not mere classification, but detection: given the ground state of an interacting Hamiltonian and a symmetry group $G$ along with its representation, is there an efficient way to tell if the state is in a SPT phase with respect to $G$? While there exist such practical tests in one spatial dimension (1D), methods in 2D have so far been restricted to finite-size systems or require an explicit form of virtual symmetries of the tensor networks representing the ground state. Here, we develop an agnostic and efficient method to detect interacting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 2D SPT phases, using an infinite projected entangled-pair (PEPS) representation of the ground state. The method is agnostic to the symmetry representation in the virtual space of the PEPS tensor and applicable independent of the bond dimension of the tensors. Moreover, it is efficient as it does not require finite-size scalings: it works directly in the thermodynamic limit. We numerically demonstrate the procedure by mapping out phase boundaries away from fixed-point wavefunctions. We extract the SPT label cocycle data explicitly from the PEPS tensor.

title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
summary: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two-dimensional charge-density field. The desired spatial distribution of the confined charge defines the target quantum-dot geometry for inverse design. The FNO reproduces charge densities with a relative $L^2$ test error of just 0.6\% and enables millisecond-scale differentiable evaluations. Relative to the CPU-based physics simulator, the FNO achieves a 17,000-fold speed-up on GPU for a single design, with further performance gains enabled by batched inference. When embedded in a gradient-based design loop with fabrication constraints, the FNO can produce both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions. The ability to engineer these distinct confinement configurations demonstrates control over quantum-dot shape and position, providing a route towards designing devices with distinct qubit-relevant operating properties prior to fabrication.

title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
summary: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

title: Thermodynamics of Forgetting in a Bounded Hopfield Network
summary: A memory that keeps learning must also forget. The Hopfield network does not: beyond a critical number of stored patterns it falls into a state of total confusion and retrieves none of them. Parisi showed in 1986 that bounding the synaptic strength cures this pathology, since the clipping of the couplings gradually erases the oldest memories and leaves room for the new ones. In this paper we provide a thermodynamic description of the resulting network, known as the Hopfield-Parisi model. Starting from the learning rule, we show that the network is equivalent to a Hopfield model whose patterns are weighted according to their age, superimposed on a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, both governed by the synaptic bound: a larger bound makes the memory longer, but also noisier. The theory of nonlinear networks developed in the eighties already provides, through the heuristic replica method, the equations that govern this model at any temperature, but to the best of our knowledge they have been solved only at zero temperature. We rederive them at the replica symmetric level through Guerra's interpolation and solve them at finite temperature, obtaining the phase diagram of the model together with its memory horizon, namely the largest age at which a pattern can still be retrieved. The solution shows that forgetting acts on the signal alone, the noise being the same for patterns of every age, and that the horizon is maximal at an intermediate bound which is essentially insensitive to temperature. Monte Carlo simulations of networks trained with the original learning rule support these predictions.

title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
summary: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory. Here we combine the truncated Wigner approximation with an asymptotic analysis, and show that this locking is produced by a slowly varying density profile through a universal mechanism, whereby the relative phase near the density maximum drifts towards zero. We show that this drift is already present in the linearised theory and its timescale is determined by the density curvature alone, while it is independent of the tunnel coupling. Rescaling time by the relaxation time scale collapses the dynamics for different system sizes and density profiles, while non-linearity suppresses the excitation returning from the edges.

title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
summary: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/π phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.

title: Exact magnetic ground states and competing interlayer exchanges in layered kagome magnets
summary: Magnetic ground states in layered kagome magnets are investigated using a Heisenberg model with six interlayer exchange interactions. For isotropic two-sublattice models with identical diagonal Fourier exchange functions, a coplanar single-wave-vector ground state is shown to exist for arbitrary exchange ranges. Extending the three-exchange model of Rosenfeld and Mushnikov reveals that longer-range interactions can change the preferred magnetic order from spiral to ferromagnetic and back to spiral, rather than merely modifying the spiral period. The analysis includes ground-state phase diagrams, harmonic stability, magnetic-field response, and sensitivity to individual exchange interactions. The propagation vector, internal layer angle, saturation field, and planar susceptibility are also found to be insufficient to determine all six exchange constants uniquely. These results provide a basis for predicting noncollinear magnetic order from first-principles exchange interactions.

title: All Bell inequalities with a quantum advantage in the minimal scenario are self-testing
summary: In the minimal Bell scenario, all extremal quantum correlations are known, but the Tsirelson inequalities that delimit the quantum set remain poorly understood. We study which correlations can maximize a given Tsirelson inequality, and conversely, which inequalities are maximized by a given correlation. We show that every Tsirelson inequality with quantum advantage is maximized by a single, extremal correlation, and thus self-tests the corresponding realization. This characterizes all self-tests based on linear Bell inequalities in this scenario. We also show that at most a two-dimensional family of inequalities can be maximized by a nonlocal extremal correlation. We identify these as polygons for a family of correlations realized by qubit states of arbitrary entanglement. This allows us to deduce that the quantum set is not self-dual.

title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
summary: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
summary: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.

title: Supermoiré Formation and Robust Topological Edge State in Helical Trilayer Graphene
summary: When two materials with nearly matched lattice constants meet, they form commensurate domains separated by incommensurate domain walls that absorb the mismatch. Recently, this picture has been extended to moiré lattices: when two moiré superlattices have nearly equal periodicities, they can form a "supermoiré" consisting of commensurate moiré domains separated by domain walls. Helical trilayer graphene (HTG) is a particularly interesting example: theory predicts that its commensurate domains are distinct topological insulators, separated by a network of conducting domain walls. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to visualize supermoiré domains and their electronic properties in HTG at a twist angle of $\sim1.7^\circ$. We find atomic-scale evidence of relaxation into supermoiré domains, each hosting flat bands separated from remote bands by large gaps of $\sim40$ meV. Domain walls exhibit spectrally uniform edge states along their length, in excellent agreement with calculations for valley-protected topological edge modes. The topological character of the flat bands is intimately tied to wavefunction localization on a graphene sublattice, and we reveal the topological change across a domain boundary by imaging the reversal of sublattice polarization.

title: Observable-Based Learning of Effective Entanglement Hamiltonians
summary: Determining the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) of an interacting quantum many-body system remains a fundamental challenge beyond special analytically tractable cases. Here we develop an observable-matching framework for learning effective EHs, which we demonstrate using response estimates from quantum Monte Carlo. As applications of this framework, we first calibrate the overall prefactor of the lattice Bisognano--Wichmann (LBW) construction using equal-time correlations and then learn spatially resolved couplings beyond its prescribed profile, without assuming a specific functional form for their spatial dependence. Trained solely on local correlations, the learned EHs reproduce benchmarked von Neumann and second Rényi entropies in $1$D and second Rényi entropies in $2$D. For a strong-bond cut associated with special surface criticality at the $(2+1)$D $O(3)$ Wilson--Fisher critical point, free-form learning outperforms the calibrated LBW ansatz in predicting the second Rényi entropy and reveals spatially nonuniform coupling renormalizations. Importantly, the learned EH also provides access to the von Neumann entropy in this setting, revealing a negative subleading correction and extending previous Rényi entropy findings to the von Neumann case. Directly evaluating the von Neumann entropy in such $(2+1)$D interacting quantum many-body systems remains challenging for conventional numerical methods. These results establish observable-based learning as a route to constructing effective entanglement Hamiltonians beyond prescribed spatial profiles in higher-dimensional interacting systems.

title: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions
summary: Free-fermion states are classically simulable, yet, written as qubits, they typically carry extensive magic, the quantum resource that stabilizer circuits lack. Part of this magic is nonlocal: local unitaries acting separately on two parts of the system cannot remove it. If these local unitaries are restricted to Gaussian ones, the nonlocal magic grows linearly with the number $m$ of partially entangled fermion pairs. We show that this growth is an artifact of the Gaussian restriction: local Gaussian unitaries minimize the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy for up to three pairs, but not from four pairs on. General local non-Gaussian unitaries that respect fermion parity take $m$ free-fermion pairs to fermionic Bell pairs with a fidelity that decays at most as $1/\sqrt m$ compared to exponential decay with Gaussian unitaries, so the nonlocal magic drops from linear to logarithmic in $m$. The reason is statistical --- Bell pairs have equal Schmidt weights, that is, a fully degenerate entanglement spectrum, and a state can stay far from them only if its Schmidt weights are spread over many orders of magnitude. This spread is measured by the capacity of entanglement $C_E$, the variance of the entanglement Hamiltonian, and the nonlocal magic of any fermionic state grows at most logarithmically with $C_E$. Free-fermion pairs add to $C_E$ independently, so $C_E$ grows only linearly in $m$, and this leads to the stabilizer fidelity decreasing at most as $1/\sqrt m$. Almost all the magic of free fermions, including Hartree--Fock and BCS mean-field states, is therefore local.

title: Thermodynamic geometry of three coupled Ising spins: exact curvature, frustration and bond anisotropy
summary: Thermodynamic curvature is widely used as a diagnostic of interactions and phase transitions, yet its interpretation is usually tested only in the thermodynamic limit. Small spin clusters are physically relevant in their own right, since a macroscopic sample of independent molecular trimers or a few-qubit quantum simulator is governed exactly by the few-spin partition function. They also provide the only setting in which the geometry can be obtained in closed form together with its full dependence on the interaction topology. We study the Fisher-Rao (Ruppeiner) geometry of three Ising spins with arbitrary pairwise couplings in a longitudinal field. This cluster interpolates continuously between an open chain and a geometrically frustrated triangle. For the symmetric triangle we obtain the scalar curvature in closed form. It vanishes on the noninteracting line and on a line of fixed field-to-temperature ratio that does not depend on the coupling, which coincides with the inflection point of the single-spin susceptibility. The near-zero behaviour is therefore exactly linear and reflects analyticity rather than critical scaling. In the frustrated antiferromagnetic regime the curvature remains finite and negative down to zero temperature. A general low-temperature formula relates this plateau to the change in magnetization content between the degenerate ground manifold and its first excitation. Any bond anisotropy destroys the plateau below a crossover temperature that depends only logarithmically on the anisotropy, so the curvature is an extremely sensitive detector of exact ground-state degeneracy. On the ferromagnetic side the zero-temperature curvature is universal for all couplings, whereas additional zero lines in anisotropic clusters track field-induced crossings of excited levels.

title: Electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium: discretization and effective medium approximation
comment: To be presented at The 10th International Scientific Conference The Modeling of Nonlinear Processes and Systems (MNPS-2026)
summary: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is $σ_1$, $σ_2$, or the harmonic mean $σ_{12}=2σ_1σ_2/(σ_1+σ_2)$, with probabilities $(1-p)^2$, $p^2$, and $2p(1-p)$, respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity $x$ and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on $p$ and the conductivity ratio $r$. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a $200\times200$ resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of $1/2$. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.

title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.

title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
summary: Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.

title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
summary: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
summary: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability $p\in[0,1]$. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to $Sp(N)$ rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for $N\ge40$, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of $Sp(N)$ under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including $SU(N)$.

title: Typical number and stability of equilibria in large non-reciprocal complex systems
summary: We consider a prototypical class of dynamics of $N\gg 1$ degrees of freedom subject to two competing terms, one favoring relaxation to a trivial equilibrium and one taking the form of a Gaussian force field promoting the emergence of many local equilibria. The latter is a non-gradient field, i.e. it includes a non-reciprocal component with a tunable strength. For this model, we compute the quenched complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the typical number of equilibria, resolved by stability index. We compare it with the annealed complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the average number of equilibria. We show that the two coincide only in the fully non-reciprocal limit: for any finite degree of reciprocity, typical realizations contain exponentially fewer equilibria than predicted by the average count. Increasing reciprocity enhances the discrepancy between the two. The quenched complexity depends explicitly on the covariance of the random force field and on the degree of non-reciprocity: the universality observed at the annealed level breaks down. The average counting of equilibria correctly identifies the location of the topology trivialization transition, but it does not capture the typical organization of equilibria near this transition, nor the stability index of the dominant equilibria.

title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
summary: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

title: Flat-band systems: A platform to realize the moments of Quantum Metric
summary: The quantum metric is a fundamental geometric property of Bloch bands that governs a wide range of physical phenomena, yet experimentally accessing it remains challenging. We show that the momentum-space variation of the quantum metric can be probed through the real-space dynamics of a Gaussian wave packet prepared in an isolated flat band. Following the application of a weak constant force, we demonstrate analytically that the leading order change in the wave-packet variance is linear in time and contains a contribution proportional to the wave-packet averaged gradient of the quantum-metric trace. This geometric contribution remains finite despite the absence of band dispersion. We illustrate the effect using a gapped Lieb lattice with an exactly flat middle band and vanishing Berry curvature, allowing the quantum-metric contribution to the spreading to be isolated. The numerical results agree with the analytical prediction and confirm the quantum-metric contribution to the wave-packet spreading. The required lattice preparation, tunable hopping amplitudes, applied force, and density measurements are compatible with established ultracold-atom techniques, providing a possible platform for observing the predicted response. Our results establish wave-packet spreading as a dynamical probe of quantum geometry in flat-band systems.

title: Ultrafast Moiré Exciton Dynamics Revealed by Two-Dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy
summary: Moiré superlattices of van der Waals heterostructures confine excitons into discrete energy levels in finite-sized samples, yet their internal relaxation pathways remain obscured by inhomogeneous broadening. Here, using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS), we directly resolve seven discrete energy levels of the moiré-confined intralayer $\mathrm{WS}_{2}$ A exciton in an hBN-encapsulated $\mathrm{WS}_{2}/\mathrm{WSe}_{2}$ heterostructure, corresponding to a confinement depth of 57.02 meV. By tracking the population of these levels over picosecond delays, we uncover a two-stage thermalization process: an effective exciton temperature drops from 171.8 to 99.3 K within 1.2 ps through rapid intra-manifold population redistribution, followed by a slower recovery toward quasi-equilibrium mediated by exciton--environment interactions. Kullback--Leibler divergence analysis confirms the progressive transition from a non-equilibrium to a Boltzmann-distributed population. Our results establish state-resolved access to moiré exciton dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring nonequilibrium many-body phenomena in moiré quantum materials.

title: Interfacial polarity control of anomalous Hall effect in LaCoO3-SrIrO3 heterostructures
summary: Interfacial polarity in oxide heterostructures can drive robust charge redistribution across the interface, yet its role in tailoring topological transport phenomena like the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) remains largely unexplored. Here, we control the sign of polarity-induced charge in SrIrO3-LaCoO3 interfaces by independently engineering the layer stacking sequence and the atomic termination. In-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy directly confirms the sign reversal of the induced charge in SrIrO3 through the contrasting electronic band shifts between different interfacial configurations. Magneto-transport measurements across a systematic matrix of four distinct heterostructures reveal that the AHE can be cleanly toggled on and off: it emerges exclusively under electron-doped conditions, while remaining suppressed for hole-doped SrIrO3. Our results establish that this response originates from an intrinsic, Berry-curvature-driven mechanism governed by polarity-controlled band filling of SrIrO3. These findings shift interfacial polarity from a passive structural consequence to an active design variable for engineering topological quantum states in oxide heterostructures.

title: Single-shot ground-state preparation via strongly coupled baths
summary: Preparing ground and thermal states of quantum many-body systems is a central task in quantum simulation. Dissipative protocols have emerged as a promising solution for both near-term and fault-tolerant hardware, but most constructions rely on weak system-bath coupling, leading to slow cooling. Here, we construct cooling protocols at strong system-bath coupling, and demonstrate accurate state preparation within even a single cooling cycle. Our protocols combine dynamically ramped ancilla energy levels with time-dependent couplings to optimize the trade-off between cooling error and physical time. For a general class of free-fermion systems, we reduce the dynamics exactly to a two-level scattering problem: ground-state cooling becomes a control problem of maximizing resonant excitation transfer while suppressing non-adiabatic heating. We then construct a family of ``Möbius-Ingham'' protocols, which reach optimal error scaling for gapless spectra and almost-exponential suppression of the leading heating error for gapped spectra, as a function of the cycle period. In our free-fermion benchmarks, Möbius-Ingham cooling lies on the Pareto frontier between steady-state error and cooling time among the controls tested. We further demonstrate its effectiveness in interacting Ising and $t$-$V$ chains and the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Finally, we extend our construction to Gibbs state preparation, showing how free-fermion thermal states can be prepared in a single cycle.

title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
comment: 43 pages, 16 figures. Submission to SciPost Physics
summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

title: Dynamical Keldysh model for colored noise and finite relaxation rate
summary: The Keldysh model describes quantum dots subjected to Gaussian noise with infinite correlation time. For multi-component noise coupled through non-commuting matrices, the spectrum exhibits a pseudogap. We solve the model for coloured noise with any correlation time, $1/ γ$. Finite memory leads to the pseudogap being filled, its peaks merging and the line narrowing.

Here we demonstrate multi-channel non-Abelian edge pumping on a silicon photonic chip by adiabatically encircling multiple band degeneracies in a multi-gap lattice. In a minimal three-band band-triangle, two opposite-charge Weyl points and one zero-charge degeneracy are linked by global band connectivity, yielding both opposite-boundary and same-boundary edge channels. Sequencing these channels produces non-Abelian braiding of three topologically protected edge modes that reside on distinct physical boundaries. The process remains fully gapped and is protected by topological winding rather than by maintained spectral degeneracies. The same band-triangle principle extends systematically to an arbitrary number of channels, establishing a scalable route to collective, sequence-controlled routing of topological states in integrated photonic circuits.

title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
summary: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
summary: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase π/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.

title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
comment: 27 pages, 23 figures: Letter (4 pages + End Matter, 3 figures) and Supplemental Material (20 figures)
summary: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench response fades, giving a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.
